evidence.notes: Two halves: the inactive-after-retries state in the row (Severity Statuses Semantic=Critical, which is distinct from the per-run Error of REQ-48 and correctly reads as more serious), and telling the creator, which is a notification. escalations.question: Are the produced PDF, the Excel workbook and the delivery email design-system surfaces that Sand builds and owns as Figma components — or are they renderer templates specified as a data-and-layout contract in developer handoff, outside the design system?
escalations.why_not_a_component_fix: No choice of component resolves it. The Sand Design System Library is an application-UI library: a full-file census across every node name and every text string, over all 14 pages and all 85 component sets, returns ZERO document, spreadsheet or email surfaces. This is not one missing component but the absence of a whole surface kind, and the answer decides what gets built rather than which component is used. It also decides whether the design system takes on print and email-safe layout, which have different constraints from everything in it today — email in particular cannot use the spacing-token model the library documents as mandatory, because transactional email is table-based and inline-styled with no CSS variables.
options: Build a shared "Report Document" component family in Figma (page frame, header block, section block, empty block, placeholder block) plus a transactional-email family, and treat Excel as a data contract only. Covers 12 of the 13 no-match requirements with reusable parts; adds print and email layout to the design system’s remit.

Treat all three surfaces as renderer templates: specify them in /developer-handoff as content and data contracts (section order, unit scaling per REQ-59, sheet naming, no-readings copy, placeholder copy) and build no Figma components for them. Fastest, and honest about Excel; but the PRD is explicit that the PDF and email are "designed surfaces in their own right, not a default wrapper", so this reads as overriding the PRD and needs to be an explicit decision rather than a default.

Split by surface: build the PDF and email families in Figma because the PRD calls them design surfaces, and treat Excel as a pure data contract because a workbook has no visual surface a person navigates.
escalations.recommended: Split by surface (option 3). It follows the PRD where the PRD is explicit and stops short of pretending a spreadsheet is a design artefact. Scope both new families as shared rather than module-specific, per the system-wide-reuse rule — any future exported document or transactional email needs the same parts.
escalations.also_depends_on: PRD claim 6 (Sand has a mail abstraction but no delivered email route) is UNVERIFIED. If there is no delivery route, the email surface has no consumer and the question partly answers itself.
escalations.no_gate_holds_this: Gate 2 reviews built components and seeds no decisions, so nothing in the pipeline will hold the work open while this is unanswered. It must be raised out loud, in the gate 2 packet, or it will surface only in the closure report — after the module is built.

library_findings.finding: The Button component set documents a Loading state that does not exist. Its handoff frame on the Buttons page states "Default, Hover, Loading, Disabled" and "Loading exists for both Default and Error — the icon slot is replaced with a spinner (Icons/General/Loading)". Enumerating all 108 children of the set (node 88:3690) gives State = Default | Hover | Disabled only, in every Semantic, Type and Size.
library_findings.why_it_matters: A direct match asserted from that documentation would be wrong, and the error would surface only during assembly. REQ-38 (generate once, on demand) needs it.
library_findings.fix: Add the documented Loading state to the shared Button set.

library_findings.finding: No focus state on the non-field controls. Button (108 variants), Checkbox, Radio Button, Switch, Flat Tab and Button Tab expose no Focused value, while all eight field families (Input Field, Text Area, Search Field, Date Picker Field, Phone Number Input, Autocomplete, Tags Input, Number Input / Stepper) do carry State=Focused.
library_findings.why_it_matters: WCAG 2.2 AA (REQ-75, decided at gate 1) requires a visible focus indicator on every interactive control. The library has a focus idiom already, so this is an omission rather than a convention — which makes it cheap to close and serious to leave.
library_findings.fix: Add Focused to Button and the four control families, matching the field families’ treatment.

library_findings.finding: The Figma Variables API is unreadable with the available credentials (/v1/files/:key/variables/local returns 403 — the token lacks file_variables:read, and the plan is starter tier). Colour and spacing tokens were read from the library’s own documented Colors and Spacing & Effects pages instead.
library_findings.why_it_matters: Token bindings can be checked by NAME but not verified by variable ID. Gate 2’s tokens_and_variables_bound check therefore rests on visual inspection rather than on a machine-readable binding.
library_findings.fix: Grant file_variables:read, or accept name-level verification at gate 2 and say so in the signoff note.

library_findings.finding: The Figma MCP server refuses this file: the account (moanes@sandbase.com) holds a View seat on a starter-tier plan, and get_metadata, get_libraries and use_figma all return "you don’t have edit access to this file". REST reads work, which is why every analysis stage in phase 2 completed.
library_findings.why_it_matters: The component pass (/figma-component-pass) and page assembly (/figma:figma-use) write through the Plugin API via MCP. Both are blocked until the account is granted edit access. This blocks the run before gate 2.
library_findings.fix: Grant the account edit access to the Sand Design System Library, or run the build passes from an account that has it.
